title: Slide a skid under a machine while it is raised no more than 30 mm
instruction: Raise the green machine no more than 3 cm, slide the wooden skid under it, and set the machine down on the skid. Don't drag the machine out of place.
context: Millwrights and machinery movers (O*NET 49-9044) raise equipment only as far as needed to get skates or a skid under it, and keep it from shifting while it is raised: a machine lifted high or dragged while up can topple, damage its feet and the floor, or trap a hand. One hand raises and holds the machine while the other slides the skid in.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Two objects. (1) Machine: a loose solid box of green painted steel standing in for a small machine, 70 mm along x, 90 mm along y, 60 mm tall, 0.30 kg, standing on the table centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0, sides parallel to x and y. (2) Skid: a loose hardwood plank, 60 mm wide (along x), 440 mm long (along y), 12 mm thick, 0.12 kg, lying flat on the table centred at x 30.0 cm, y -27.0 cm, long side along y. It spans y -49.0 cm to -5.0 cm, so its left end stops 5 mm short of the machine's right side. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial. It keeps the largest horizontal distance of the machine's centre from its starting mark ('drift'), the greatest height above the table top reached by any point of the machine's underside ('raise'; a tilted machine counts by its raised edge), and the machine's largest tilt. 'The skid lies flat' means its downward face is within 3 mm of the table top and it is tilted less than 3 degrees (either broad face up). 'On the skid' means the skid lies flat, the centre of the machine's underside is within 2 mm of the skid's top, the machine is tilted less than 3 degrees, and at least 75% of the machine's footprint is over the skid. 'The skid is under the machine' means the skid lies flat, at least 50% of the machine's footprint is over it, and the centre of the machine's underside is no more than 3 mm below the skid's top (so the skid is beneath the machine, not beside it). Score 0 if at any moment the machine tilts more than 30 degrees or its drift exceeds 30 mm (dragged out of place, or carried over to the skid instead of the skid being brought under it), or if it ends off the table (its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top). Otherwise: 1.0 if the machine ends on the skid, its drift never exceeded 10 mm and its raise never exceeded 30 mm; 0.75 if it ends on the skid with a raise of at most 50 mm but outside the 1.0 limits; 0.5 if it ends on the skid but was raised more than 50 mm; 0.25 if the skid is under the machine but the machine is not on it (still held up, resting on less than 75% of its footprint, or leaning on the skid's end); 0 in every other case (the machine back on the table, the skid beside it or on top of it). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with both objects still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, the raise is read from a side video against 30 mm and 50 mm marks on a card standing upright 10 cm behind the machine (a measuring aid only, out of the arms' way), and the drift against 10 mm and 30 mm outlines taped round its starting place.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction; both objects slide on the bare table. The machine is a plain solid box with no feet, anchors or lifting points, and the skid a single rigid plank; there are no rollers, skates, jacks or pry bars: the grippers raise the machine and push the skid directly.
reset_notes: Put the machine back on its mark centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0, and the skid back flat on the table centred at x 30.0 cm, y -27.0 cm, long side along y. Nothing is consumed.
